roadmapStep: Absolute supervisor stage B1 (local build) after the B1 design record DP1P_SUPERVISOR_B1_LOCAL_2026-10-18
method: Each tool was built by a coder in its own new directory as a derived copy with a reverse-replace diff proof against its accepted base, then verified by an independent tester; tools with high-risk logic also had an Opus architecture auditor, and the host-adjacent tools (AD-P3B, W4B) had a Fable second opinion confirmed by root or Opus before use. Root read every packet, re-derived the key diffs and wrote a decision record for each acceptance. Interrupted runs were kept as untrusted partial directories and rebuilt in fresh directories.

keyRules: The prior review that lets the next window start is written only from a separate root acceptance record that names the prior job, case, receipt, window decision hash, review tool pin, review output hash and class, and only for the next case in the order C01, NORMAL PASS, TERM PASS
Behaviour job identifiers carry their case, and the chain ledger must list C01 first, then each earlier behaviour job in case order, ending with the stage-one prior job
The review's window class comes only from the post-window review output, and the review's controller block comes from the prior release review
The window contract case must equal the GO, job configuration and receipt case wherever the case is trusted

dryRuns.synthetic: Every result class (PASS, NONPASS, UNKNOWN, NOT_EXECUTED), a GO_CAP refusal and a NORMAL -> TERM -> KILL chain reached the post-window review through the real pinned tools; only the remote target, the A03 remote and the behaviour launcher were stubs
dryRuns.realTurn: DRY-1 started: run d1 (NORMAL) passed with the single operations worker and a live root decision. Root turn 13.7 s, GO age 18.7 s of the 75 s cap, ticket-to-claim 2.3 s of 25 s, runner pre-contact 1.5 s of 4 s, adapter 2.4 s of 10 s. Four more consecutive passing runs are required; the count must be re-established under any new root, because root turn time belongs to the commander.
dryRuns.budgets: The runner's 4 s pre-contact budget and the adapter's 10 s budget are kept with a quiet-machine rule: dry runs and real windows run with no other agent or heavy local process; a quiet-machine run over 3 s or 7 s respectively opens a budget review before any real window

limits: All work was local with synthetic inputs; real signal delivery, timeout exit codes and target behaviour can be shown only in the B2 windows
The P3B behaviour launcher is never executed in dry runs (the operations session denies its hash in SYNTHETIC mode); the real C01 metadata launcher preflight of about 2.8 s is the reference

A local runner refusal before any contact is classed UNKNOWN rather than NOT_EXECUTED (the runner's refusal line has six keys and the review expects seven); this cannot produce a false pass, but UNKNOWN stops B2 for an owner decision
A remote that stalls until the transport timeout ends UNKNOWN by design
The prior-review tool has not yet been run on the real C01 records; that is the first step of NORMAL preparation
next: Finish DRY-1 (five consecutive green real-turn runs including TERM and KILL), then prepare NORMAL: the C01 acceptance record, prior review on the real C01 inputs, a fresh admission A04, stage one on real inputs, the real window contract and a GO request; the NORMAL window then needs a fresh owner GO
